title: Silas and the Portrait
premise: Estate lawyer Beatrix Galloway is summoned to read the will of Silas Merrick, a reclusive painter who supposedly died a decade ago—yet the will is dated three days ago, and the portrait that accompanies it depicts Beatrix in clothes from their own closet. When a stranger's body surfaces dressed in those same stolen garments, Beatrix realizes someone has been living inside their life, studying them through the case files of an old unsolved death. As investigators circle and the killer anticipates every move, Beatrix traces Silas's forged identity to a twin brother who faked his own death to escape a crime he witnessed—and who now needs Beatrix, the only person who can authenticate the will, dead or discredited. In the climactic confrontation inside Silas's sealed studio, Beatrix turns the killer's obsession with the case file against him, baiting him into confessing before witnesses hidden among the canvases, and inherits not the estate but the burden of deciding which version of Silas's memory deserves to survive.
about_author: Rafael Vasquez spent fifteen years as a probate clerk in coastal New England before turning to fiction, drawing on the strange, half-buried lives he encountered in dusty estate files. He writes mysteries about paper trails, inherited secrets, and the people who read other people's endings for a living.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Beatrix Galloway opens a probate file for Silas Merrick—a man whose death certificate is ten years old—and finds a freshly signed will naming Beatrix personally as witness and executor. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into personal dread as the ink smells of yesterday.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Stranger
chapters.summary: At the Merrick house, Beatrix uncovers a canvas depicting themselves in exact detail, wearing a gray coat from their own closet. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: violation—the sensation of being watched for years by eyes that never blinked.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Police pull a drowned man from the harbor dressed in Beatrix's stolen coat, face ruined beyond recognition. Detective Ilsa Vann suspects Beatrix. POV: alternating Beatrix and Vann. Emotional beat: fear hardening into defiance as Beatrix realizes invisibility is over.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix digs into the original 2014 file on Silas Merrick's first 'death' and finds their own younger signature on documents they never signed. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past has been edited, and Beatrix was edited into it.

chapters.title: The House Remembers
chapters.summary: Searching the shuttered studio, Beatrix finds layers of portraits: dozens of strangers, each painted in clothing later found on corpses across two decades. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: horror reframed as pattern—the killer isn't improvising; he's completing a series.

chapters.title: Detective Vann's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vann shares an off-the-record theory: the drowned man died before the coat was taken, meaning the killer dresses bodies after death—to stage scenes from paintings. POV: Vann. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between hunter and suspect.

chapters.title: Letters to a Dead Man
chapters.summary: In the estate safe, Beatrix finds unsent letters from Silas to his twin brother Ambrose, written after the faked death, full of guilt over something witnessed at Gull Point lighthouse. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief for a man who erased himself to survive.

chapters.title: The Case File Knows
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into Beatrix's office and leaves the original case file open to a page only the killer should know—annotated in Beatrix's own handwriting style. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: paranoia; the enemy is writing Beatrix into the record.

chapters.title: Gull Point
chapters.summary: Beatrix travels to the lighthouse where the twins grew up and meets a retired keeper who recalls 'Silas' returning changed after one stormy night in 2013. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the past acquiring weight and weather.

chapters.title: Ambrose
chapters.summary: Records reveal Ambrose Merrick died in 2013—or so the paperwork says; Beatrix finds evidence he assumed Silas's identity after witnessing a fatal accident involving a powerful local family. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: sympathy twisting toward suspicion—which twin survived?

chapters.title: The Second Portrait
chapters.summary: A new painting arrives at Beatrix's apartment: Beatrix asleep, rendered from inside the room. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: terror made intimate; the watcher has been inside.

chapters.title: Vann Closes In
chapters.summary: Vann matches the drowned man to a missing archivist who once catalogued the Merrick estate, and warns Beatrix they are next on the canvas. POV: Vann. Emotional beat: urgency compressing the timeline to days.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: A document examiner confirms the new will is genuine—but signed by a hand trained to imitate both twins, meaning the writer learned forgery from their father, a sign painter. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the mystery narrowing to bloodline and inheritance of craft.

chapters.title: What the Family Buried
chapters.summary: Beatrix confronts the local family implicated in the 2013 accident; the matriarch admits paying hush money and reveals a third sibling no record mentions. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as debt passed down like property.

chapters.title: The Third Twin
chapters.summary: Beatrix identifies the hidden sibling—raised apart, erased from the wills, the true heir with motive to resurrect both brothers' names. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by doubt; the answer fits too neatly.

chapters.title: Frame
chapters.summary: Evidence implicating Beatrix surfaces—forged letters, planted fibers—and Vann must arrest or trust them. POV: Vann. Emotional beat: betrayal and loyalty colliding; Vann chooses trust on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Baiting the Brush
chapters.summary: Beatrix leaks a false claim: the original 2013 case file has been found and will be authenticated publicly at the studio. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into strategy—using the killer's obsession with the file as a hook.

chapters.title: Night in the Studio
chapters.summary: The trap springs; the third twin—living for years as the estate's quiet caretaker—arrives to destroy the file and finds Beatrix waiting among the portraits. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: stillness before violence, two invisible people finally seen.

chapters.title: Confession in Oil
chapters.summary: Cornered, the killer confesses: the drownings were recreations of the 2013 accident, each body a rehearsal until the final portrait—Beatrix—could make the family pay. Hidden recorder and Vann capture everything. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: catharsis edged with pity for a life spent as a copy.

chapters.title: Which Memory Survives
chapters.summary: With the killer held, Beatrix must authenticate or void the will, deciding whether Silas's erasure or Ambrose's guilt becomes the legal truth. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the weight of authorship over another's memory.

chapters.title: Executor
chapters.summary: Beatrix voids the forged will but petitions to preserve the studio and its portraits as testimony, giving the victims' names back to the record. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: mourning converted into memorial.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Canvas
chapters.summary: Months later, Beatrix visits the restored studio, finds one last unsigned sketch of themselves—alive, unhidden, walking away—and leaves it hanging. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: release; visibility chosen at last, the portrait finally a lie.
